what_this_is: The 2026-09-16 re-audit's central finding is not that individual guards were wrong. It is that guards were written where production does not go. A guard whose reach nobody states is a guard whose reach nobody can lose, so reach is DECLARED here, per guard family, and tools/certification/guard_reach.py refuses a declaration that is not checkable. A status is a declaration about what the code does, not a summary of what a grep found: nothing here is inferred.

statuses.REACHED: a production entry point reaches the rule and a named test exercises it there
statuses.LIBRARY_ONLY: the rule exists and no production entry point reaches it. This is a FINDING and must name the improvement that will close it
statuses.LATENT: the rule guards a shape that does not occur in the tree at all, so there is nothing to reach yet. Not the same as unreached, and must say what would create it

production_entry_points: the domain runners under engcore.domains (thermal_models, electrical.dc, battery, kinetics.cstr, repair)
residuals: This is the REACH map for the guard families whose reach the audit measured by R-xx, not a complete guard inventory. The inventory is tests/mutation_guards.py's job and the Core Freeze V4 round's (I-30).

The four bypass checks are SYNTACTIC. A bypass written in a shape none of them matches -- a dynamic dispatch, a getattr, a call through an alias the checker does not resolve -- is not caught. Each row says per check what it cannot see rather than claiming completeness.
The verifier reads src/engcore only. A bypass in benchmarks/, in a script or in a test is not production and is not checked.

guards.title: A grid rebuild turns an unassessed or incomplete uniqueness search into a SUPPORTED one-mode grid
guards.rule_symbol: route_uncertainty (the rebuild branch, which runs the canonical MultistartPolicy() itself where a grid route is in play and the caller supplied none)
guards.why: The rule is right and there is nothing in the tree for it to reach: route_uncertainty has no caller in src at all. The one production study reaches the V2 gates through grid_predictive_uncertainty directly (see R-02) rather than through the router, so the rebuild shape does not occur in production today. That is LATENT and not LIBRARY_ONLY: LIBRARY_ONLY would say a production path bypasses the rule, and no production path asks for a rebuild.
guards.what_would_create_it: a production call to engcore.hybrid_uq.router.route_uncertainty. I-13 (binding routed predictions to calibration content) and I-07 (grid evidence the supplier cannot steer) are where a routed production path would arrive; on that day the ROUTE_UNCERTAINTY_REBUILD_WITHOUT_MULTISTART check turns the audited shape -- a rebuild policy passed together with multistart=None, which asks for the rebuild while declining the search -- into a build failure instead of a SUPPORTED one-mode grid.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: a rebuild policy reached through a variable the checker cannot resolve (policy = None; ...; route_uncertainty(rebuild=policy, multistart=policy2)), and a caller that passes a multistart argument whose value is a None-valued name rather than the literal None.

guards.title: The production calibration study predicts and validates through frozen V1 functions, so no V2 evidence gate runs
guards.rule_symbol: grid_predictive_uncertainty (CORE-006 route claim and evidence judgement) over grid_goodness_of_fit (CORE-001), grid_containment (CORE-002), require_grid_is_this_evidence (CORE-005) and grid_prior_uniformity (CORE-010)
guards.why: Batches 17 and 18 routed engcore.studies.calibration_study -- the only production consumer of the predictive layer -- through grid_predictive_uncertainty, so every production prediction, held-out verdict and coverage repetition now passes the V2 evidence gates before the frozen V1 interval is formed: a grid the router would not route RAISES, and a grid it routes with a finding DOWNGRADES the claim and carries the reasons onto the record. Residual, stated rather than hidden behind the status: the study is the only production path that predicts at all. The MCP tools run solvers and report credibility; they form no predictive interval, so there is no second production path for this rule to reach.

bypass_allow_list_reasons.src/engcore/uq/predictive.py: it IS posterior_predictive_uq. The frozen V1 function applies only the grid-resolution refusal, which is exactly why a direct consumer of it is the audited shape.
bypass_allow_list_reasons.src/engcore/hybrid_uq/predictive.py: grid_predictive_uncertainty calls the frozen function AFTER judging the grid -- route claim, evidence judgement and prediction-domain reasons first, interval second. Wrapping it is the fix, so the wrapper is the one caller that is meant to be here.
bypass_allow_list_reasons.src/engcore/adequacy/predictive.py: the CORE-011 content binding applies grid_containment and grid_prior_uniformity to the posterior before it will bind, and withholds the binding on a finding (batch 17). It does NOT apply grid_goodness_of_fit: a content binding is about whether the grid is THIS posterior's evidence, not about whether the model fits, and the fit statement belongs to the verdict the binding is attached to. That omission is a residual BATCH17's protocol states, and this allow-list entry is where it stays visible.

guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: a consumer that reaches the frozen function through an alias (f = posterior_predictive_uq; f(...)), through a getattr, or through a re-export the checker does not resolve back to this name.

guards.title: The CORE-014 operating-point binding never fires in production and is bypassable when enabled
guards.rule_symbol: ScientificModelDefinition.assess_validity(record_values=...) and ValidityAssessment.evaluated, bound by ScientificResult._require_assessment_is_about_this_model and CredibilityEvidenceReport._require_assessments_at_this_operating_point
guards.why: record_values defaults to False on a V1-frozen symbol's method and before batch 14 NOTHING in src passed True, so the CORE-014 binding looped over an empty mapping on every production path. Batch 14 set the default to True on DomainValidityContext.assess -- the domains' own helper, and the path battery, electrical and repair all assess through -- and passed it explicitly at the conduction and KCL sites, so a result or a credibility report now refuses a verdict made at a different operating point than its own provenance states. Residual, recorded on the report rather than hidden: 59 of the 77 condition names across the 16 registered models are reserved DERIVED quantities and 18 are declared inputs, so most names cannot be bound by name at all; they are REPORTED in CredibilityEvidenceReport.unbound_assessment_values and not counted as agreements (D-14-1). An interval verdict binds only the values that did not move within the step, so a coupled battery step binds its state of charge and current and not its temperature.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: an assessment built by hand rather than through assess_validity -- a ValidityAssessment(...) constructor call with an empty `evaluated` -- and an assessment produced outside src/engcore/domains. The first is what the MCP boundary's registry check and the model-id/version binding are for; the second is not production. The check also cannot see a call that passes record_values=False, which is a DECLARATION that the caller does not want the bytes: the shape it finds is a caller who never considered the question.
guards.note_on_the_empty_allow_list: BATCH19's preregistration expected domains/derived_context.py on this allow-list, because its own default is True. It is not needed: that method forwards `record_values=record_values` to assess_validity, so the checker sees the name in the argument list and the site is not a hit. An allow-list entry that is not needed is a hole nobody would notice, so the list is empty and the expectation is recorded as an amendment in the protocol instead.

guards.title: CROSS_SOLVER_VALIDATED is guarded only by string checks, and non-independent disagreement is absorbed as WARNING
guards.rule_symbol: TrustedConsensusGate.assess, which requires byte-verified artifact independence before CrossSolverConsensus.to_check may keep the CROSS_SOLVER_VALIDATED level
guards.why: CLOSED by I-12 part B (batch 25), and this row is what says so. `TrustedConsensusGate` had no caller in src: the one production consensus check was minted in engcore.mcp.problem from `CrossSolverConsensus.to_check`, which reaches the scientific comparison and the string-declared independence and never the gate. It is now built BY the gate. That path ships no artifact digests, so the gate withholds CROSS_SOLVER_VALIDATED and records the withholding structurally, and the boundary's own `_withhold_level` still runs for its own different reason -- the check is about values it does not scope to -- so the level is withheld twice over and either rule alone would leave it one change away from a report. Two more halves of R-21 closed with it: every check carrying the level must now name exactly one `independence basis:` -- `declared` (verified against the domain layer's pin) or `artifact-verified` (the gate's byte-digested line) -- which is what the audit meant by a reader being unable to tell the two apart; and a disagreement beyond tolerance is now FAIL whether or not the routes are verified independent, so the audited 33% case no longer reads WARNING under a SUPPORTED verdict. R-21's first claim -- hand-written evidence lines earning the level -- was already closed by VAL-01 and is pinned by a test of its own. Residual, stated rather than hidden behind the status: `artifact-verified` is unreachable in production, because no production route ships artifact digests, so the production path awards nothing at all.
entry_points: engcore.mcp.tools.run_electrothermal (the cross-solver check emitted when a second route is asked for) -- reaches TrustedConsensusGate, which withholds the level for want of artifact bytes, and then the boundary's own _withhold_level
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: a to_check call whose _withhold_level wrapper sits further than 40 characters before it, which the checker reports rather than allows. The production path no longer has such a call at all: the check it emits is the gate's. What no static check can see is a check COPIED from a genuine consensus onto another result -- it carries a genuine threshold record and a genuine basis line -- which needs the check bound to the result it qualifies (CORE-009/VAL-01, I-20's).

guards.title: UncertaintySource never reaches a verdict or report, and SRIA budgets accept NUMERICAL as model-form
guards.rule_symbol: UncertaintySource and the source_kind it declares on a StandardUncertainty
guards.why: UncertaintySource has no producer in src, so source_kind is UNSPECIFIED on every uncertainty production makes. Batch 8's I-09 gave the credibility report an `uncertainty` field, so the TRANSPORT now exists and reaches production; what does not exist is any production site that declares where the number came from. That matters twice: a budget cannot tell a numerical-discretization term from a model-form term, which is what lets an SRIA budget accept NUMERICAL as model-form; and an UNSPECIFIED kind is indistinguishable from a kind nobody was asked for, so the gap is invisible at the point of use. I-25 is where the producers declare it and the field records re-derive what they claim.
entry_points: engcore.mcp.evidence.CredibilityEvidenceReport.from_result (reached by run_electrothermal and run_battery) -- carries the uncertainty, with source_kind UNSPECIFIED on every production record
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: nothing static: this row declares a MISSING producer, and no syntactic check over the tree can distinguish an uncertainty whose kind is genuinely unknown from one whose producer never declared it. That is exactly why the reach is declared here and measured by I-25's own tests rather than by a scan.

guards.title: Cross-domain crossings carry bare point values, and UncertaintyTransfer binds nothing
guards.rule_symbol: UncertaintyTransfer, which binds a crossing quantity's propagated uncertainty to the transfer that produced it
guards.why: The problem is REACHED in production -- the audit's own value, and why this row's audit_reached_in_production is `yes` -- while the GUARD is not. The production electrothermal coupling passes bare point values across the thermal/electrical boundary with no uncertainty, no validity state and no validation state attached, and UncertaintyTransfer, the record that would bind them, has no caller in src. So a crossing that loses its uncertainty loses it silently: the receiving domain sees a number, and nothing downstream can tell a propagated quantity from a declared one. This is the one row where LIBRARY_ONLY understates the risk rather than overstating it, because the unguarded path is the one production actually runs. I-27 is where the transfers carry uncertainty and validity with physically bound checks.
entry_points: engcore.mcp.tools.run_electrothermal (the thermal/electrical coupling) -- passes bare point values and reaches no UncertaintyTransfer
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: nothing static: a crossing that passes a float is a call the checker could find only by knowing which arguments are crossing quantities, which is a type question and not a syntactic one. I-27's own tests are what will measure it once the transfers exist; until then this row is the declaration that they do not.

guards.title: Quantity.parse evaluates unit expressions, magnitudes accept bool or str, and delta units pass as absolute
guards.rule_symbol: Quantity.parse and Quantity.__post_init__ over _declared_magnitude, _require_the_unit_is_a_unit_and_not_arithmetic, _require_the_magnitude_written_is_the_magnitude_parsed and is_delta_unit; the delta refusal itself is src/engcore/mcp/problem.py::_read_quantity
guards.why: Every declared value in an MCP run_electrothermal or run_battery payload is read by _read_quantity, which calls Quantity.parse and now also refuses a delta unit where the binding's unit_exemplar is absolute. The reproductions run through build_electrothermal_problems on the SHIPPED example payload rather than through the parser alone, which is what makes the row REACHED rather than LIBRARY_ONLY. Residual, stated rather than hidden behind the status: the grammar is about TEXT, so a caller constructing Quantity(5.0, 'volt') in process bypasses it entirely -- as it must, that being the two-argument path the class is built on -- and only __post_init__'s bool/str rule reaches there. The library comparisons that also mishandle offset scales (R-48, R-52, R-57) are parts B and C of this improvement and are LIBRARY_ONLY until then.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: a boundary other than _read_quantity that reads a declared unit and checks only its dimension. The delta rule is applied at one call site, not enforced structurally, so a second such reader would have to consult is_delta_unit itself -- which is why parts B and C put the rule into the library comparisons rather than leaving it at the boundary.

guards.title: The consensus verdict depends on route order through the first route's unit
guards.rule_symbol: CrossSolverConsensus.from_results' canonical common_unit (base_unit of each quantity's dimension) and its is_ratio_scale refusal, over _compare, relative_difference and _floored_difference; the same rule in src/engcore/scientific/oracles.py::_same_operating_point
guards.why: LATENT rather than REACHED, and the distinction is the point of this ledger. Both rules sit on code production runs -- the only production caller of from_results is engcore.domains.electrical.dc_consensus, and _same_operating_point is read by ScientificResult's CORE-009/CORE-014 validity binding -- but neither production path can currently present the SHAPE the rules are about. DC lists the native route first and reports on volt and ampere, both coherent SI units, so the canonical conversion is the identity and no recorded magnitude or digest moves; no production result states an operating point on an offset scale. So the fix is real and the guards are exercised, in the library, by the tests below. Claiming REACHED would be claiming a production exercise that does not exist, which is the assertion I-16 was written to stop.
guards.what_would_create_it: A second caller of CrossSolverConsensus.from_results whose routes report one name in different units of the same dimension -- which is the ordinary case the moment an external provider reports in its own units rather than the native route's -- or any production result that states an operating point on an offset temperature scale, degC being the unit an engineer writes.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: CrossSolverConsensus.over, which takes bare numbers and has no units to canonicalise. It cannot award CROSS_SOLVER_VALIDATED (IND-02), so what it records is a measurement rather than a claim -- but a caller reading its worst relative difference is reading whatever scale it handed in.

guards.title: The corner-agreement guard compares magnitudes in each law's own unit
guards.rule_symbol: _require_corners_agree, over CORNER_AGREEMENT_REL_TOL: both meeting laws' magnitudes converted into base_unit(definition.unit) before the difference is taken
guards.why: LATENT rather than REACHED. require_complete_boundary IS reached -- the conduction2d domain calls it -- but no shipped 2D declaration states two edges of one field in different units of the same dimension: they state kelvin throughout, so the conversion is the identity and the guard's behaviour on production declarations is unchanged. The guard is nevertheless the production refusal, and the audit records what its absence cost: in conduction2d the corner node is pinned to whichever edge the assembly writes last and the domain's own boundary_conditions_held check reports FAIL -- a contradiction found after the solve rather than refused before it, and found only because that domain happens to check. A consumer relying on the core refusal got nothing.
guards.what_would_create_it: Any declaration that states one field's edges in more than one unit of its dimension -- a plate whose ambient side is given in degC and whose heated side in kelvin, which is how an engineer would write it -- or a field declared in degC, whose corner agreement was judged on a scale whose zero is a convention.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: Two edges that agree at every corner and disagree along a shared span. They cannot share a span on a structured quadrilateral, so there is nothing more to compare here -- but that is a property of this support type, not a general one.

guards.title: Spreads on offset temperature scales convert as absolute temperatures
guards.rule_symbol: require_spread_unit and Quantity.magnitude_as_spread_in over _slope_against_base, plus Quantity.to's wrapping of a backend scale refusal; applied at every declared spread in the core -- OracleObservation.absolute_tolerance, ConstraintDefinition.tolerance and the margin its check reports, GaussianObservation.sigma as read by ObservationSet.numeric_vectors and by inference/split.py's two content digests, and PredictiveObservableSpec.observation_sigma
guards.closed_by: I-22 parts D (batch 29, the audit's finding 58) and E (batch 30, finding 99)
guards.why: FIXED, in two batches. R-48 is one defect at four sites and every site needed a conversion the units module did not have: a difference transforms by the linear part of an affine map, and `magnitude_in` applies the whole map. Part D gave the module `magnitude_as_spread_in` and `require_spread_unit`, wrapped the backend's scale refusal in this package's own error, and fixed the oracle tolerance. Part E applied both primitives at every other DECLARED spread, which is what part D's own version of this row named as the reason it stayed PARTIAL: `require_spread_unit` is applied at call sites, and nothing structurally requires a spread field to consult it. Now every spread field in `src/engcore` does. LATENT rather than REACHED: `ConstraintDefinition` is reached by every MCP rating and limit check, `GaussianObservation` by the production calibration study and by `studies/tcr`, `PredictiveObservableSpec` by the predictive layer the study routes through -- and all of them are reached with RATIO-SCALE units, ohm, watt, kelvin, ampere, so every conversion is the identity and no production number moves. What is reached is the guard; what is latent is the offset-scale declaration that would trip it.
guards.what_would_create_it: Any declaration that states a tolerance, a sigma or a band on an offset temperature scale -- '2 degC' as a limit tolerance and '0.5 degC' as a measurement sigma are how an engineer and a lab respectively write them, and the first let a 600 kelvin reading satisfy a 358.15 kelvin limit while the second gave a 50 kelvin misfit a chi-squared of 0.033. Or any field, bound or observable declared on an offset scale, where an absolute unit cannot carry the spread or the margin at all.
entry_points: engcore.mcp.problem (rating and limit checks, via ConstraintDefinition.check)
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: A spread read with `magnitude_in` DOWNSTREAM of a declaration. `studies/calibration_study.py`, `studies/tcr.py`, `adequacy/predictive.py`, `hybrid_uq/predictive.py` and `uq/predictive.py` do so at several points; those reads are safe because the declaration guard admits only ratio-scale units, where the two readers agree exactly -- but they are safe BY that guard and not by their own statement. And a `Quantity` handed around loose still carries no statement of whether it is a point or a span: what this improvement adds is that every declared spread FIELD makes that statement at construction.

guards.title: A posterior cut at the declared upper bound, with data bounding only the lower side, is SUPPORTED
guards.rule_symbol: _rebuild_grid's per-side bound-domination test over _GAUSSIAN_BAND_SD = sqrt(2 * EDGE_LOG_LIKELIHOOD_DROP), beside the existing both-sides rule; and src/engcore/hybrid_uq/local_gaussian.py::_clamp_leverage_cumulant, the I-14 part that had to land first
guards.closed_by: I-06 (batch 31); the batch also closes I-15's last open conformance case
guards.why: LATENT. The rebuild path is reached only by a caller that supplies both a MultistartPolicy and a table builder: the production calibration study routes a SUPPLIED grid and the MCP tools form no predictive interval at all, so no production path can present the shape. The rule is nevertheless fixed in the router because that is where the width a claim reports is decided. What this closes is the width a SUPPORTED claim WOULD report if such a caller arrived -- 2.372, 2.788 and 3.522 for one set of data at declared upper bounds of 40, 60 and 80. Note that the leverage-null clamp shipped in the same batch IS on every local route, production included; it is carried on I-14's row when that lands, and is recorded here because R-11 could not be exercised at all without it.
guards.what_would_create_it: Any caller that rebuilds a grid from a local covariance -- the documented way to get a posterior when the supplied grid is refused -- on a problem where the data constrain a parameter from one side only. A decay rate whose signal is gone inside the observation window is the ordinary case: every rate above some value predicts the same thing, so the upper side is whatever was declared.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: The refinement regime, and deliberately. A posterior the data HAVE localised but which a declared bound truncates still reports a width that depends on where the bound is -- 0.6712, 0.8912, 1.129, 1.341 and 1.699 at bounds of 11, 12, 13, 14 and 16 -- because the moments of a truncated distribution do depend on the truncation, and the audit's own fix direction asks for that path to be kept. The line between the two regimes is the 5.2565 sd band distance and it is drawn on purpose; BATCH31_THRESHOLD_PROTOCOL.json states both sequences so the choice is visible.

guards.title: An evidence-binding mismatch raises instead of passing over
guards.rule_symbol: grid_is_this_evidence (returns) beside require_grid_is_this_evidence (raises), and the router's supplied-grid path consulting the first
guards.why: LATENT. The production calibration study supplies a grid it built itself in the same process, so the binding it faces is its own and cannot disagree; the MCP tools supply no grid. The rule is nevertheless what decides whether a request survives a fact about its grid, which is why it is fixed at the router and not left to a caller's try/except.
guards.what_would_create_it: Any caller that supplies a grid a DIFFERENT process computed -- which is what supplying a grid is for. A solver converged to 1e-9 relative against observations with sigma 1e-4 relative is enough: that is about 1e-5 of a sigma per residual, ten times the 1e-6 the binding allows, and it aborted the whole request.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: Which NODES the binding re-evaluates, and that the supplier chooses them. R-19 is I-07 part B and is OPEN: a supplier who keeps the checked rows honest can still sharpen the posterior bulk, and now gets PASSED_OVER rather than a raise when caught -- which is this part working, not a weakening of that one.

guards.title: The uniform-prior step tolerance refuses a grid that is effectively uniform
guards.rule_symbol: grid_prior_uniformity's moment-effect bound over _reweighted_moment_shift and PRIOR_REWEIGHT_MOMENT_SD
guards.why: LATENT, and this row is about a claim newly ALLOWED rather than newly refused, which is the direction this round is normally careful about. No production path supplies a grid on an axis whose spelling disagrees with its declared transform, so nothing production does changes. The bound is measured rather than assumed, and the detail records how far the moments actually moved.
guards.what_would_create_it: Any caller that supplies a grid spaced in natural units for a LOG-declared parameter -- which is what `numpy.linspace` gives you, and is how the audited case arose. Its prior density varied about 4% and its moments matched the accepted spelling's to six digits.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: The reweighting's effect on the FIRST TWO moments of each axis marginal. A node density that leaves both alone and distorts a tail, or a correlation, is not caught. The first two moments are what a grid route REPORTS, so they are what the rule is about -- but this is not a statement that the prior is uniform.

guards.title: Evidence binding spot-checks 8 nodes, 4 of them seeded from the supplier's bytes
guards.rule_symbol: _spot_check_rows over SPOT_CHECK_WEIGHTED_ROWS and SPOT_CHECK_INADMISSIBLE_ROWS, with a verifier-side nonce and every face's highest node; the same rule in src/engcore/hybrid_uq/router.py::_require_table_agrees_with_forward
guards.why: LATENT. The production calibration study supplies a grid it built itself in the same process, so the binding it faces is its own and there is no supplier to be adversarial; the MCP tools supply no grid. The threat the rule is about is a grid computed elsewhere, which is what supplying a grid is FOR -- so this is the guard on the feature rather than on a current caller.
guards.what_would_create_it: The first caller that supplies a grid, or a rebuild table_builder, that another party computed. The audited forgery needed no privileged access: keep the four fixed rows honest, sharpen the bulk, and nudge one far-tail log-likelihood by 1e-9 until the four seeded rows miss it. Two attempts, and the result was GRID_AS_SUPPLIED SUPPORTED with every reported width halved.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: A tampered region holding LESS than a quarter of the posterior weight: 17 weighted draws catch a 10% region about 83% of the time, not 99%. The rule states a detection probability against a stated fraction and claims no more; certainty needs the audit's other alternative, re-evaluating every node within ln 1e6 of the peak, at a cost proportional to the grid. And the weighted draw uses the GRID's own weights, so a forger who lowers the weight of what they tampered with reduces their chance of being drawn -- but that lowering is itself the tampering and moves the moments the route reports, which is what the honest-versus-forged comparison measures. The circularity is real and bounded, not absent. Separately, the REBUILD path's weighted draw has no forgery reproduction here (mutation B33h is a declared survivor): the audit asserted that path's exposure in one sentence without measuring it.

guards.title: assess_routed_identifiability accepts loosened thresholds on the local route
guards.rule_symbol: assess_routed_identifiability's local branch calling _require_declared_or_tighter_thresholds, _tightened_note, and RoutedIdentifiability.__post_init__'s canonical-threshold refusal and re-derivation of that note
guards.why: LATENT. The router calls `assess_routed_identifiability` with its defaults, so no production path passes a threshold at all and nothing production does changes. What R-28 is about is the PUBLIC function and the record it returns: a caller who calls it directly, or who serializes what it returns, could obtain a verdict the declared rule does not give -- and the record read back, because it was self-consistent.
guards.what_would_create_it: Any caller that passes an identifiability threshold. The thresholds are arguments on purpose, so that a study may be STRICTER, and that is exactly why the loosening direction had to be refused rather than documented: the same argument on the same problem's GRID has always raised `looser than the declared 1.0`.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: `confidence_level`, which is not one of the declared thresholds: it selects WHICH interval is measured rather than how wide one may be, so a caller who asks for a 50% interval gets narrower relative widths and can reach a better verdict that way. The report carries the level and the grid branch refuses anything but 0.95 outright; the local branch's freedom is deliberate, because closing it is a different rule than the one R-28 names. And the guard is on the THRESHOLDS -- a caller who hands in a posterior whose covariance is wrong still gets a verdict consistent with that covariance, which is R-25's and R-27's territory.

guards.title: Local RouteDiagnostics read-back trusts carried fields
guards.rule_symbol: _require_reasons_follow_measurements: the policy-with-starts rule, the NaN-tail-ratio rule and the observation-count-against-the-digest rule; RouteDiagnostics.observation_content_digest under hybrid_uq.route_diagnostics/3; require_posterior_matches_observations, called by the local route; engcore.inference.split.observation_set_content_digest. Claim (b)'s closure is the pre-existing mass-ratio rule together with the uniqueness re-derivation.
guards.closed_by: I-14 parts C (batch 35: claims (b), (c), (d)) and D (batch 36: claim (a), with the route_diagnostics/3 bump)
guards.why: FIXED, and REACHED -- the first of I-14's parts that is. `require_posterior_matches_observations` is called by `local_gaussian_posterior` on the record it has just built, so every posterior the router produces is verified against the observations it was fitted to while both are in hand; the production calibration study routes the local posterior. Without that call the binding would be a read-back rule, and a read-back rule is checked by whoever chooses to check. The read-back half remains library-only for the reason every read-back is: nothing in production reads a posterior back from a payload it did not just write, and `from_dict` exists so that a READER can check one -- which is what R-22 is about, the check being the product.
guards.what_would_create_it: Any reader that takes a serialized posterior from elsewhere. The record is designed to travel and its reasons are re-derived on read precisely so a reader need not trust the sender; the audited forgeries need only consistent numbers. The observation count was the extreme case -- one integer, read by the goodness of fit and by nothing else, so no other field disagreed with an edit from 10 to 40.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: The tail rule is a NECESSARY condition only: a record with a FINITE ratio that no probe actually produced is not caught, because nothing ties the ratio to the probes. Binding that needs the probe outcomes in the record, which is a schema question. And BETTER_OPTIMUM vs SECOND_MODE is still not re-derived from the objective although all three numbers are there -- deliberately not added, because LOWER_OBJECTIVE_SAME_BASIN vs SAME_OPTIMUM cannot be re-derived at all (its tolerance is 2 * gradient @ cov @ gradient, which the record does not carry), and half a rule is worse than a stated gap. And a `route_diagnostics/2` payload carries no digest, so its observation count is unbound and R-22(a) survives for such a payload -- deliberately: refusing it would break records this core wrote three batches ago, the route now writes `/3` for everything, and the schema string says which shape a reader is holding.

guards.title: Renaming the parameterization or moving recorded bounds escapes the HUQ-12 bound-distance check
guards.rule_symbol: require_posterior_matches_calibration, called by local_gaussian_posterior; and HybridUQResult._require_one_truth's declared-parameterization rule in src/engcore/hybrid_uq/router.py
guards.why: REACHED, because the calibration binding is called by the LOCAL ROUTE on the record it has just built -- and the production calibration study routes the local posterior. The audit calls R-25 library-only because the forgeries are read-back forgeries, and the read-back half is indeed library-only; what is REACHED is the binding that makes every record the route writes verified against the request it came from.
guards.what_would_create_it: Any reader that takes a serialized posterior from elsewhere. The first forgery needed one string: renaming the parameterization to 'linear_map:anything' makes the bound-distance re-derivation return after a single check, because a mapped posterior's diagnostics describe its parent by design. The second needed the bounds and the covariance moved together, which preserves every distance in sd units.
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: A record read WITHOUT its calibration: the bounds-moved forgery survives that reading, and it cannot be closed from inside the record. Declared bounds are a property of the REQUEST, every field is the forger's to edit, and a digest the forger can recompute binds nothing. What the batch does is make every record the ROUTE writes verified, and give a reader holding the calibration the one function that checks it.

guards.title: Grid HybridUQResult read-back and prediction trust hand-built records
guards.rule_symbol: _considered_problems and the rebuilt-record misfit and structural rules in HybridUQResult._require_one_truth; _grid_diagnostic_problems and grid_record_variance_shrink_window in src/engcore/hybrid_uq/identifiability.py, the second stating the limit the others cannot close; the `_refused` observation content digest in src/engcore/hybrid_uq/local_gaussian.py; RouteReason.GRID_NOT_BOUND_TO_EVIDENCE on routed_predictive_uncertainty (batch 37, finding 24)
guards.closed_by: I-14 parts E (batch 37, finding 24) and F (batch 38, finding 22)
guards.why: LATENT, not LIBRARY_ONLY: every rule here guards a record shape that does not occur in the tree. The router never writes a ledger without its used route, a rebuilt record over a misfit posterior, or an effective sample size V1 would have refused; and the only non-test caller of `HybridUQResult.from_dict` (benchmarks/core_v2_hybrid_uq/audit/kinetics.py:267) reads a record it produced itself in the same process. The audit's own verifier reached the same reading: 'No MCP or evidence path takes these records from outside.' PARTIAL rather than FIXED because two of finding 22's five claims are provably not closable from a record alone and are stated as a number instead -- see the residual below. One part of this batch IS reached: `_refused` now writes the observation content digest, so the local route, which the production calibration study uses, no longer returns a record `from_dict` refuses.
guards.what_would_create_it: Any reader that takes a serialized routed record from outside the process that produced it -- a cached grid record replayed across runs, or an evidence path that accepts one over the MCP boundary. The forgeries need no cryptography: the digests a record carries are integrity-only and anyone can recompute them, which is why the rules re-derive instead.
entry_points: engcore.hybrid_uq.local_gaussian.local_gaussian_posterior (reached by engcore.studies.calibration_study) -- the `_refused` digest half only
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: A grid record's moments and identifiability are BOUNDED on read, not re-derived: the grid is data-plane and is not serialized. Inside `grid_record_variance_shrink_window` (7.98 on the audited record) the covariance can be divided and nothing contradicts it; relative widths lowered with the covariance or lowered alone are undetectable, because no lower bound on a central 95% interval follows from a standard deviation; and a small shift of the mean is undetectable for the same reason the digests are integrity-only. Closing any of these needs the grid's own marginal quantiles carried in the committed summary, which is a schema bump and an owner's decision -- recorded as the batch's open decision.

guards.title: GUARD 21 compares signed residual and tolerance
guards.rule_symbol: comparison_met_its_bound, which now compares abs(residual) with the tolerance; and the negative-tolerance refusal in ValidationCheck.__post_init__
guards.why: REACHED, and more strongly than the audit's 'library-only' suggests: the rule is on `ValidationCheck.__post_init__`, so every check the domain gates build passes through it, and run_electrothermal and run_battery run those gates on their way to a verdict. The audit calls R-46 library-only because the forgery is a hand-built check, which is true of the CONSTRUCTION; the rule itself sits between a production entry point and a published number, because a level that `comparison_met_its_bound` clears is what `attained_levels` reports into the credibility report.
entry_points: engcore.mcp.server.run_electrothermal and run_battery, through the domain validation gates that build every ValidationCheck
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: `outcome` is still refused rather than derived: `abs(residual) <= tolerance` is necessary for a PASS and not sufficient, and a refinement gate in this repository FAILs with a residual inside its bound because the sequence behind it never contracted. So a check that reports FAIL or NOT_RUN while its numbers agree is still constructible, deliberately, and a non-finite tolerance is still constructible on those outcomes -- the finiteness rule makes the comparison False, so nothing can claim success on one.

guards.title: The CORE-013 status precedence changed without a schema bump
guards.rule_symbol: REPORT_SCHEMA at validation_report/2 with LEGACY_REPORT_SCHEMA still read; _legacy_status and _legacy_status_read; ValidationOutcome.NOT_APPLICABLE, its refusal of a declared level and its exclusion from ValidationReport.status; ValidationReport.not_applicable; the NOT_APPLICABLE outcomes and the conditional validation_requirements in src/engcore/domains/electrical/dc/{validation,problem}.py; NumericalCritic's named-checks detail in src/engcore/sria/assurance/critics.py (batch 39); uncertainty/2 and its refusal of a /1 payload carrying source_kind in src/engcore/scientific/results/uncertainty.py; validity_assessment/3, _ASSESSMENT_BINDING_KEYS and the matching refusal in src/engcore/scientific/models/definition.py; hybrid_uq.routed_identifiability/2 with /1 refused for a stated reason in src/engcore/hybrid_uq/identifiability.py

guards.why: REACHED. `ValidationReport.status` is read by `CredibilityEvidenceReport` on the way to a verdict, so run_electrothermal and run_battery reach it; the DC gate and the DC problem builder are production code on that same path, and the batch's own test drives a solve end to end. The audit's 'library-only' describes the READ side of the problem (a stored report from an older tree), which is where a user's saved result comes in; the status rule itself was never library-only. FIXED as of part C, which closed finding 90's items 2 and 3: a record carrying one of the newer bindings now declares a version an older reader refuses, so the binding can no longer be dropped in silence, and a pre-CORE-004 identifiability record is refused for the reason it cannot be read rather than for a contradiction it does not contain.
entry_points: engcore.mcp.server.run_electrothermal and run_battery, through the domain validation gates and CredibilityEvidenceReport.from_result
guards.what_the_check_cannot_see: A `/1` payload whose stored status matches neither precedence is refused, and the reader still cannot tell a hand-edit from a third precedence nobody recorded -- version strings are the only signal, which is the point of the bump. `validation_check` is not versioned here, so a bare check payload carrying `not_applicable` is refused by an older reader on the enum rather than by a version check. And only the DC gate distinguishes the two outcomes: other domains' 'did not apply' checks still report NOT_RUN, and src/engcore/domains/thermal/** is SHA-256 pinned and cannot be edited. On the reverse direction: `local_gaussian_posterior/1` and `hybrid_uq_result/1` are still refused through their embedded route diagnostics rather than by an outer version check, and the V4 serialization inventory (I-30) is where these compatibility events become executable fixtures. A digest remains no authority: re-emitting a record through any writer gets that writer's version, and the protection is only that a newer field cannot ride under an older version.
